title: Plan capacity for uncertain traffic growth
notice: All system measurements, costs, incidents, and growth ranges are invented for evaluation.
decision: Choose a capacity investment plan for the next 12 months before the next quarterly planning lock.
objective: Keep p95 request latency below 400 ms and monthly availability at or above 99.9% while avoiding premature fixed spend.

options.label: Keep current architecture and respond to alerts
Add observability and staged scaling thresholds

constraints.text: p95 request latency must remain below 400 ms at the monthly peak.
Monthly availability must remain at or above 99.9%.
Incremental infrastructure and implementation spend cannot exceed USD 180000 in the 12-month horizon.

inputs.text: Peak traffic may grow between 2x and 10x over 12 months.
The current system has passed a synthetic load test at 3x current peak but has not been tested beyond it.
A major data-tier change needs 10 to 14 weeks of engineering lead time.
Caching and query work may add 1.5x to 2.5x headroom, but the effects are not additive without testing.

important_unknowns: Current bottleneck under representative peak workload
Traffic shape, write ratio, and tenant concentration
Real scaling curve and saturation point beyond 3x
Growth leading indicators and forecast error

expected_output_properties.text: Separates traffic growth from workload shape and system efficiency instead of using one optimistic/base/pessimistic axis.
Includes a rapid-growth or concentrated-load future and a lower-growth or efficiency-gain future.
Evaluates every strategy in every scenario against latency, availability, spend, and lead-time constraints.
Does not multiply uncertain optimization gains or claim capacity above the tested 3x point as fact.
Recommends measurements or load experiments before irreversible build-out where feasible.
Defines a trigger early enough to accommodate the 10-to-14-week lead time.

prohibited_shortcuts: Inventing production telemetry or claiming the system supports 10x
Treating 2x to 10x as a probability distribution
Ignoring workload shape or implementation lead time
